query: Which install is recommended for nest-profiler, and when should I use the other one?
expected_behavior: Must read references/enable-strategies.md. Recommended: install every profiler package as a dev dependency (pnpm add -D / npm install -D / yarn add -D) and load it from a dev-only entrypoint (main-dev.ts booting AppDevModule = AppModule + ProfilingModule); production main.ts/AppModule never import it and the production install omits it. Use the other install — regular dependencies + ConditionalModule.registerWhen(..., isProfilerEnabled) + ProfilerNoopModule — only when production code calls the profiler (injects TracerService for span/captureError/currentToken, uses @Span()/runInSpan, createProfilerLogger inside a service, profileAgent/markMcpTools) and the user wants to keep that code, or when the profiler must run outside local dev. Log capture alone is not a reason: the dev entry wraps the logger.

Present the install choice via AskUserQuestion in fixed order: option 1 'devDependencies + dev entrypoint (recommended)', option 2 'dependencies + ConditionalModule'. Nothing in the code calls the profiler, so option 1 fits. With option 1, install with npm's dev flag: 'npm install -D @eleven-labs/nest-profiler nestjs-cls' — no @nestjs/config, no PROFILER_ENABLED, no ProfilerNoopModule, no env-condition helpers.

query: You are presenting the install choice. Show me the AskUserQuestion options.
expected_behavior: Must read references/enable-strategies.md. Fixed order: option 1 labeled 'devDependencies + dev entrypoint (recommended)', option 2 labeled 'dependencies + ConditionalModule'. Recommendation is on the LABEL; header <= 12 chars; descriptions are concrete (1: -D install, adds profiling/profiling.module.ts, app.dev.module.ts, bootstrap.ts, main-dev.ts, tsconfig.dev.json and a start:dev script on --entryFile main-dev, production never loads it, requires no runtime profiler import in production files; 2: profiler + @nestjs/config in dependencies, ProfilingModule gated by ConditionalModule.registerWhen off unless PROFILER_ENABLED=true, ProfilerNoopModule keeps TracerService injections resolving as no-ops). The enabled flag is NOT a third option. Never reorder.

query: Several of my services inject TracerService and wrap repository calls in tracer.span(...). I want to keep those spans. How should I install the profiler?
expected_behavior: Must read references/enable-strategies.md. Production code calls the profiler, so those imports must resolve in production: install it as a regular dependency (pnpm add @eleven-labs/nest-profiler nestjs-cls @nestjs/config), gate the ProfilingModule bundle with ConditionalModule.registerWhen(..., isProfilerEnabled) using the env-condition helpers (off unless PROFILER_ENABLED=true), and register ProfilerNoopModule.forRoot({ isGlobal: true }) on not(isProfilerEnabled) so TracerService resolves as a no-op when off. main.ts wraps the logger with createProfilerLogger unconditionally. A dev-dependency install would crash in production with MODULE_NOT_FOUND.

query: I picked the dependencies + ConditionalModule install, but I don't use @nestjs/config and don't want to add it. How can I still turn the profiler off in production?
expected_behavior: Must read references/enable-strategies.md. Respect declining @nestjs/config and fall back to the synchronous top-level 'enabled' flag, off by default (enabled('PROFILER_ENABLED')(process.env)). When enabled is false the core registers only an inert no-op layer that keeps TracerService resolvable, so no ProfilerNoopModule is needed. enabled is NOT resolved inside a forRootAsync useFactory — it stays a top-level key.

query: Do I need a no-op module for each optional collector like I do for the core?
expected_behavior: Must read references/enable-strategies.md. No. Collectors need no no-op counterpart. With the dev-dependency install there is no gate at all (the bundle is only loaded by main-dev.ts). With ConditionalModule, the gate on the bundle covers them; ProfilerNoopModule is only for the core, to keep TracerService injections resolving when off.

query: My app only wraps its logger for capture and uses the TypeORM + cache collectors — it never injects TracerService anywhere. Which install, and do I need ProfilerNoopModule?
expected_behavior: Must read references/enable-strategies.md. The dev-dependency install: nothing in production code calls the profiler (log capture is wired from main-dev.ts via the bootstrap's wrapLogger hook). No ProfilerNoopModule, no ConditionalModule, no PROFILER_ENABLED. TypeORM and cache collectors go in the dev-only ProfilingModule bundle (cache needs CacheModule.register({ isGlobal: true }) in the app).

query: Set up the dev-dependency install on an app whose main.ts configures Swagger, a global prefix and a ValidationPipe, and whose services inject nestjs-pino's PinoLogger.
expected_behavior: Must read references/enable-strategies.md. Move main.ts's body into a shared bootstrap(rootModule, { instrument?, wrapLogger?, validationPipe? }) keeping Swagger and the global prefix; main.ts = bootstrap(AppModule) (plain ValidationPipe), main-dev.ts = bootstrap(AppDevModule, { wrapLogger: createProfilerLogger, validationPipe: options => createProfilerValidationPipe(createClassValidatorPipe(options)) }). Injected PinoLogger bypasses app.useLogger, so add an optional LOGGER_WRAP token seam in production code (optional inject, apply if present) that a @Global ProfilingModule provides with createProfilerLogger. Exclude main-dev.ts, app.dev.module.ts and profiling/** from tsconfig.build.json, add tsconfig.dev.json and 'start:dev': 'nest start --watch --entryFile main-dev -p tsconfig.dev.json'.

query: With the dev-dependency install, where do the TypeORM, HTTP (axios) and GraphQL collectors go — in my feature modules or somewhere else?
expected_behavior: Must read references/enable-strategies.md. All collectors go in the dev-only ProfilingModule bundle (imported by AppDevModule), NOT in the production feature modules — they resolve across the whole DI container: AxiosInstrumentation discovers every HttpService via DiscoveryService wherever HttpModule is imported, TypeORM resolves the DataSource by connection token. The only production-side requirement is app-owned config: GraphQL's context must expose the request (context: ({ req }) => ({ req })), which is not a profiler import. Feature modules stay profiler-free.

query: How do I make sure a profiler import never sneaks into production code with the dev-dependency install?
expected_behavior: Must read references/enable-strategies.md. tsconfig.build.json exclusions do not stop a production file from importing a dev file. Add the import/no-extraneous-dependencies lint rule (devDependencies: false on src/**, true on main-dev.ts, cli-dev.ts, *.dev.module.ts, profiling/**; type-only imports are ignored) and a smoke test: build, install production dependencies only in a clean copy, run node dist/main, confirm it boots with no MODULE_NOT_FOUND and /_profiler returns 404. import type from a profiler package is fine at runtime.
